modules.name: Node canvas and typed ports
modules.design_question: Which browser node-canvas library and typed-port scheme lets designers wire Layer 0 and module outputs together safely, accessibly, and without wiring mistakes reaching execution?
inputs: User edits: add node, connect, move, group, collapse
Layer 0 payload type ids (geometry, program tags)
outputs: Graph document JSON: nodes {id, module@version, params, enabled}, edges {fromPort, toPort}
Port-type registry (nominal type id to JSON Schema $id)
Connection-rejected events with the expected type

parameters.name: connection_rule (exact type id | declared subtype | via converter node)
parameters.relationship: Stricter rule -> fewer invalid wires reach execution but more converter nodes for the user. React Flow lets the app veto a connection before it is created (isValidConnection).

parameters.name: cycle_policy (reject at connect time)
parameters.relationship: A cycle -> no topological order exists, so the graph cannot execute; blocking the wire at connect time keeps the graph a DAG.

parameters.name: port_cardinality (item | list | tree)
parameters.relationship: Tree ports (path -> branch -> item) let one module evaluate many floors or towers in one run, as Grasshopper data trees do; adds a concept users must learn.

parameters.name: canvas_library (xyflow | Rete | Baklava | litegraph)
parameters.relationship: A maintained library with a large user base lowers forced-migration risk; an archived or stale one raises it. Observed push dates and weekly downloads are in the metrics.

parameters.name: collapsed_groups (hidden flag)
parameters.relationship: Collapsing node trees through the hidden property -> fewer rendered nodes -> lower re-render cost on pan, zoom and edit.

parameters.name: handle_size and non-drag alternative
parameters.relationship: Handles under 24 CSS px, or drag-only wiring, fail WCAG 2.2 AA -> keyboard, touch and motor-impaired users cannot build graphs.

metrics.name: Canvas interaction latency (INP, 75th percentile)
metrics.method: Measure Interaction to Next Paint on drag, connect and param edit with a web-vitals style observer in the test build.
metrics.basis: web.dev Core Web Vitals INP bands; our application to a canvas editor is an adaptation, since the bands are defined for page-load field data.

metrics.name: Pointer target size of handles and buttons
metrics.good: >= 24 x 24 CSS px (or spacing exception)
metrics.bad: < 24 x 24 CSS px without an exception
metrics.method: Automated DOM measurement of every interactive element plus manual review.
metrics.basis: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), Level AA.

metrics.name: Single-pointer or keyboard alternative to drag
metrics.good: Every drag action (connect, move, resize) has an alternative
metrics.method: Checklist test; implement click-to-connect and keyboard connect commands.
metrics.basis: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, Level AA. The understanding page does not mention node editors, so applying it here is our reading.

metrics.name: Non-text contrast of ports, wires and status chips
metrics.good: >= 3:1 against adjacent colours
metrics.method: Automated contrast check of the theme tokens in light and dark mode.
metrics.basis: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast, Level AA.

metrics.name: Invalid connections accepted by the canvas
metrics.method: Property test: random pairs of ports must be accepted only when the type rule allows.
metrics.basis: Course requirement that outputs are typed inputs of the next node; zero tolerance is our policy.

metrics.name: Canvas library maintenance health
metrics.good: Not archived and pushed within 90 days
metrics.bad: Archived, or no push for more than 12 months
metrics.method: Read GitHub pushed_at and archived flag; npm weekly downloads for adoption. Observed 21 Oct 2026: xyflow pushed 2026-10-20 (8.35 M downloads/week); Rete pushed 2026-10-18 (47 k); Baklava pushed 2026-09-16 (1.7 k); litegraph.js pushed 2024-08-01; Comfy-Org litegraph fork archived (pushed 2026-01-14).
metrics.basis: Threshold days are an editable team preset; the observed values are verified.

metrics.name: Interactive node/edge capacity at 60 fps on a mid-range laptop
metrics.good: unverified: to be benchmarked
metrics.method: Benchmark with synthetic graphs of increasing size; React Flow's performance guide gives no node-count figures.
metrics.basis: No published sourced figure found.

visualization: The canvas itself: node cards with a category colour stripe (13 taxonomy codes), a title, ports on left (inputs) and right (outputs), and a status badge (verified / team assumption / FALSE ASSUMPTION in its reserved colour).
Ports coloured and shaped by type (circle = item, square = list, diamond = tree) with a collapsible legend; colour is never the only cue.
A rejected connection shows a red dashed ghost wire and a tooltip 'expects Layer0.Geometry, got Table'.
Minimap and collapsed group frames; auto-layout button.
modules.method: Build on @xyflow/react. Custom node components are generated from manifests (P15-M03); each Handle carries a nominal port-type id (the $id of a JSON Schema). isValidConnection rejects: a type mismatch without a declared converter, a cycle (walk getOutgoers from the target), and a second wire into a single-cardinality input. The graph JSON (nodes, edges, parameters, enabled flags) is the single source of truth; React Flow keeps only view state. Memoise node components, keep derived state such as selected ids outside the nodes array, and collapse groups with the hidden property. Provide click-to-connect and keyboard connect commands, 24 px handles and 3:1 contrast. Auto-layout with dagre. Keep the React Flow attribution visible unless a Pro subscription is bought.

libraries.name: @xyflow/react 12.12.0
libraries.role: Primary node canvas (custom nodes, handles, validation hooks, minimap)

libraries.name: rete 2.0.6
libraries.role: Fallback canvas plus dataflow engine if React is dropped

libraries.name: @baklavajs/core 2.8.1
libraries.role: Vue-based alternative with engine and interface types

libraries.name: @dagrejs/dagre 3.1.1
libraries.role: Auto-layout of the DAG

libraries.name: elkjs 0.12.0
libraries.role: Optional layered layout for large graphs (licence needs review)

libraries.name: litegraph.js (original) - NOT recommended
libraries.role: Rejected: last push 2024-08-01; Comfy-Org fork archived

modules.effort: Core: about 1.5 dev-weeks for canvas, typed ports and status badges; +3 days accessibility pass (team estimate).
modules.human_judgment: Maintainers decide the port-type vocabulary, category colours and what counts as unit-compatible; the designer decides which wires express the design intent.
modules.limits: Nominal type ids avoid structural JSON Schema subset checks but need a maintained type registry. WCAG bands are applied to an editor by our interpretation. Node capacity is unmeasured. React Flow attribution terms and Pro pricing (Starter $169/month, Professional $289/month at retrieval) can change.
jury_criteria: No direct jury criterion; enabler for all four tags (human_scale_40, cultural_context_30, design_excellence_20, urban_integration_10).

modules.name: DAG execution, run-all vs step-into, provenance
modules.design_question: How does the tool run a wired graph deterministically, let users run everything or step into one node, and log inputs, thresholds and sources so every result shows its work?
inputs: Per-node enabled flag and user threshold overrides
outputs: RunRecord JSON: run_id, graph hash, per node {module@version, parameter values, input hashes, outputs, metrics with threshold basis and source ids, status flag, duration, error}
Typed node results consumed by downstream nodes
Stale/blocked status map for the canvas

parameters.name: execution_mode (auto | run-all | step-into)
parameters.relationship: Auto keeps results fresh but recomputes on every edit; run-all gives the user control over cost; step-into exposes one node's inputs, parameters and thresholds for audit. Design choice; no sourced evidence on trust effects.

parameters.name: cache_key = hash(module@version, parameters, upstream hashes)
parameters.relationship: Same key -> reuse the cached output; changed key -> recompute only that node and descendants. Rete's dataflow engine caches outputs and requires an explicit reset when inputs change.

parameters.name: topological schedule (Kahn)
parameters.relationship: Ordering nodes so each runs after its inputs costs O(V+E); edges left over after the queue empties reveal a cycle, so a cyclic graph is refused.

parameters.name: port cardinality (item | list | tree)
parameters.relationship: Whether a module runs once or once per branch depends on the input structure; trees map paths to branches of items.

parameters.name: disabled-node mode (bypass | block)
parameters.relationship: Bypass forwards type-compatible data, so downstream metrics keep computing on different inputs; block marks descendants blocked. The choice changes what a downstream pass/fail means. Design logic.

parameters.name: timeout and cancel
parameters.relationship: Longer budget -> fewer false kills on heavy modules but a longer stall; Pyodide can be interrupted from a worker with a SharedArrayBuffer, which needs cross-origin isolation headers, else terminate the worker.

parameters.name: threshold_override (editable team assumption)
parameters.relationship: Editing a threshold changes the cache key of every dependent node, so the new run is recorded with the value actually used.

metrics.name: Determinism
metrics.good: 100% identical output hashes on two consecutive runs with the same inputs and versions
metrics.method: Run twice in CI with canonical JSON serialisation (sorted keys, fixed float precision) and compare hashes.
metrics.basis: Course requirement that results show their work; threshold is our policy.

metrics.name: Provenance completeness
metrics.good: 100% of result values carry module@version, parameters, input hash, threshold basis and source id/status
metrics.method: Schema check of every RunRecord entry.
metrics.basis: Course requirement: every result cites its source and shows its work.

metrics.name: Scheduling cost
metrics.good: O(V+E)
metrics.method: Kahn or DFS topological sort.
metrics.basis: Standard algorithm complexity.

metrics.name: Main-thread responsiveness during a run (INP)
metrics.method: Run heavy modules in workers; measure INP during run-all.
metrics.basis: web.dev INP bands (adapted to an editor).

metrics.name: Incremental re-run time after one parameter change
metrics.method: Wall-clock of re-run with warm cache on the reference VTC graph.
metrics.basis: Editable preset; no sourced benchmark.

visualization: Node status chips (idle, stale, running, ok, warn, error, blocked) and a pulse travelling along wires during a run.
Bottom timeline (Gantt) of per-node durations.
Step-into side panel in three columns: Inputs (hash, preview) | Method, parameters, thresholds with source links | Outputs with pass/fail badges.
Run-diff table between two RunRecords and a 'download provenance' button.
modules.method: Load the graph, validate it against manifests (P15-M03), Kahn-sort it and reject cycles. For each node compute the cache key; on a hit reuse the stored output, otherwise call the module runtime (P15-M04), validate inputs and outputs with Ajv against the declared JSON Schemas, and append an entry to the RunRecord. Run-all executes the full order; step-into pauses before a chosen node, shows inputs, lets the user edit parameters and thresholds, then resumes. A failed node marks descendants blocked, never ok. Disabled nodes follow their mode (bypass or block). Results are immutable; any edit creates a new run. Canonical JSON and fixed float precision make determinism testable.

libraries.name: rete + rete-engine 2.0.6
libraries.role: Pull-based dataflow engine with caching, or use as a design reference

libraries.name: comlink 4.4.2
libraries.role: Worker RPC for running nodes off the main thread

libraries.name: ajv 8.20.0
libraries.role: Runtime validation of node inputs and outputs (draft 2020-12)

modules.effort: Core: about 1.5-2 dev-weeks including run-all, step-into, cache and RunRecord export (team estimate). The simple on/off toggle ships here.
modules.human_judgment: The designer chooses which modules to enable, whether to override a threshold, and whether a pass/fail verdict means anything for the design; the tool only computes and logs.
modules.limits: Cross-browser floating-point determinism is unverified for numerically heavy modules. Cache keys ignore changes in external data. Step-into is our UX design, not a standard. Time budgets are untested presets. Auto vs manual mode effects on user trust have no sourced evidence.
jury_criteria: No direct jury criterion; supports evidence traceability for all four tags (human_scale_40, cultural_context_30, design_excellence_20, urban_integration_10).

modules.name: Module manifest and validator
modules.design_question: What manifest makes every module self-describing, source-cited and machine-checkable, so thresholds, assumptions and licences are validated before a module can run or be published?
inputs: Taxonomy enumerations (13 category codes, 5 phases, 4 jury tags)
outputs: Validated manifest object
Port-type registry entries
Lint report (errors and warnings)
Module-card data for palette, registry and review (P15-M05, P15-M06)

parameters.name: id and name rules
parameters.relationship: A unique lowercase id keeps forks distinct and saved graphs resolvable. VS Code requires lowercase names, Obsidian a unique id, Yak restricted characters, crates.io case-insensitive collision checks.

parameters.name: version (SemVer 2.0.0)
parameters.relationship: The number encodes change impact: a backward-incompatible input/output schema change must raise MAJOR, so graphs pinned to a MAJOR keep working.

parameters.name: category, phase, jury_tags (enumerations)
parameters.relationship: Category decides palette placement and colour; jury tags let a dashboard aggregate which criteria a graph evidences. VS Code similarly limits categories to a fixed list.

parameters.name: inputs / outputs as JSON Schema 2020-12
parameters.relationship: Typed ports derive from schemas; changing a schema changes which wires are valid, so a schema diff drives the version bump.

parameters.name: parameters[] with relationship text, unit, source_ids
parameters.relationship: Making the causal relationship a required field stops a module from hiding assumptions; empty relationship -> lint error.

parameters.name: metrics[] with good, bad, status, source_ids
parameters.relationship: Status enum (verified | team_assumption | unverified | false_assumption_corrected) decides chip colour and whether a source is mandatory.

parameters.name: licence (SPDX expression)
parameters.relationship: The declared licence decides who may fork and redistribute; a missing licence means no reuse rights.

parameters.name: permissions[] and runtime tier
parameters.relationship: Each declared permission widens what the sandbox grants; a new permission in an update forces re-approval, as Chrome does.

parameters.name: engines (platform version range)
parameters.relationship: Declares compatible platform versions so incompatible modules are not loaded, as VS Code's engines.vscode field does.

metrics.name: Manifest schema validity
metrics.good: 0 validation errors
metrics.method: Ajv validation at editor save, registry CI and graph load.
metrics.basis: CI gate policy; validator mechanism is standard JSON Schema.

metrics.name: Threshold classification coverage
metrics.good: 100% of thresholds have status verified (with at least one opened source), team_assumption, or unverified
metrics.bad: Any unclassified threshold, or verified without a source
metrics.method: Lint rule over metrics[].
metrics.basis: Course requirement: unsourced thresholds appear as editable team assumptions.

metrics.name: SemVer compliance
metrics.good: No breaking input/output schema diff without a MAJOR bump
metrics.bad: Breaking diff shipped as MINOR or PATCH
metrics.method: Compare two manifest versions' schemas (removed or narrowed fields, changed types) and compare with the bump.
metrics.basis: SemVer 2.0.0 rule: backward-incompatible API change -> MAJOR; released versions are immutable.

metrics.name: Licence field validity
metrics.good: Valid SPDX expression; code licence is OSI-approved
metrics.method: Parse with spdx-expression-parse; check against the SPDX list with its OSI-approved flag.
metrics.basis: SPDX License List identifiers and OSI flag.

metrics.name: Source link health
metrics.good: All source URLs resolve at CI time
metrics.bad: Any 404 or 403 without an archived copy
metrics.method: HEAD requests in CI; opened flag recorded per source.
metrics.basis: Team policy; several sources in this packet returned 403, so a fallback is needed.

metrics.name: Test presence
metrics.good: >= 1 passing fixture per metric
metrics.method: Run fixtures in Vitest; compare outputs with expected values.
metrics.basis: JOSS requires an automated test suite or documented manual tests; a numeric coverage threshold is deliberately not set because none was sourced.

visualization: Manifest editor form with live inline validation (red/green).
Module card in the palette: category stripe, version, SPDX badge, and a stacked bar counting verified / team assumption / unverified thresholds.
Per-threshold chip linked to its source; FALSE ASSUMPTION chips in the reserved colour with the old value struck through and the corrected value beside it.
Lint report grouped by severity.
modules.method: Define the manifest as a JSON Schema (2020-12) with enumerations for category (13 codes), phase (basic, advanced, present, platform, cross-cutting), jury tags (4) and metric status (4). Validate with Ajv at three points: editor save, registry CI (P15-M05) and graph load (P15-M02). Ports reference named type ids; actual payloads are validated at run time. A manifest-diff tool compares two versions and suggests MAJOR, MINOR or PATCH. Lint rules: at least one opened source per verified threshold, non-empty relationship text per parameter, SPDX licence, declared permissions, at least one fixture per metric, SemVer version, unique id. Dependencies and graph pins use SemVer ranges via the semver package.

libraries.name: ajv 8.20.0
libraries.role: JSON Schema 2020-12 validator

libraries.name: semver 7.8.5
libraries.role: Version parsing and range resolution

libraries.name: spdx-expression-parse 5.0.0
libraries.role: Licence expression validation

libraries.name: vitest 5.0.5
libraries.role: Module fixture tests in CI

modules.effort: Core: about 1 dev-week for schema, Ajv wiring and lint; v1: +1 week for the manifest-diff tool (team estimate).
modules.human_judgment: Whether a source really supports a threshold, whether a relationship statement is true, and whether category and jury tags fit remain reviewer decisions; the linter checks presence and format only.
modules.limits: Validation proves shape, not truth: a wrongly sourced 'verified' passes lint. Ajv does not decide whether one JSON Schema is a subset of another, so compatibility uses nominal type ids. Fields such as i18n, icons and dependency conflict resolution are not specified here.
jury_criteria: No direct jury criterion; the status field is what makes evidence honest across design_excellence_20 and the other tags.

modules.name: Sandbox for community code
modules.design_question: How can the platform run community-contributed module code without exposing user models, tokens or the host page to malicious or buggy code?
inputs: Module bundle and manifest (runtime tier, permissions)
Validated input payload (JSON or transferred ArrayBuffer)
outputs: Schema-validated module output
Telemetry {cpu_ms, peak_memory, terminated, denied_calls[]}
Permission-grant record per module@version

parameters.name: runtime_tier (T0 declarative | T1 JS in QuickJS-WASM or SES | T2 Pyodide in isolated worker | T3 server container)
parameters.relationship: Higher tier -> more expressive (Python, native libraries) but larger attack surface and heavier load. Pyodide alone is not a security boundary, so T2 needs host-level isolation and maintainer review.

parameters.name: granted_permissions (network, storage, geometry read/write)
parameters.relationship: Default-deny plus declared permissions: each added permission enlarges what a compromised module can read or exfiltrate. Chrome warns users and disables an extension until it accepts a newly added permission.

parameters.name: origin isolation (separate origin; iframe sandbox without allow-same-origin)
parameters.relationship: Same-origin content with both allow-scripts and allow-same-origin can remove its own sandbox attribute -> no isolation; a unique opaque origin blocks cookies and storage access.

parameters.name: worker CSP
parameters.relationship: A worker is generally not governed by the creating page's CSP; unless its own response carries a CSP header, code in the worker can still use eval and the network.

parameters.name: memory, stack and time limits
parameters.relationship: Caps stop runaway modules; QuickJS offers memory, stack and interrupt-deadline limits, whereas SES does not mitigate memory or CPU exhaustion.

parameters.name: cross-origin isolation (COOP and COEP headers)
parameters.relationship: Needed for SharedArrayBuffer-based Pyodide interrupts; static hosts that cannot set headers need a service-worker shim, with a page reload on first load. Side effect on third-party embeds is unverified.

metrics.name: Sandbox-escape suite pass rate
metrics.good: 100% of red-team cases blocked (ctypes, Emscripten exports, fetch, DOM, storage, parent postMessage, eval)
metrics.method: CI red-team suite per tier, seeded with the failure classes from the Aug 2026 Pyodide disclosure.
metrics.basis: Policy threshold; failure classes verified in the Cyera report (seven products affected, including n8n CVE-2025-68668).

metrics.name: Permission least-privilege
metrics.good: Used permissions equal declared permissions
metrics.method: Instrument host API calls; compare with manifest.
metrics.basis: Chrome guidance to request only permissions the main function needs.

metrics.name: Runaway-module containment
metrics.good: Module killed within its budget; UI INP <= 200 ms
metrics.bad: UI INP > 500 ms or module not killable
metrics.method: Infinite-loop fixture; watchdog calls Worker.terminate, which stops a worker immediately.
metrics.basis: INP bands from web.dev; terminate semantics from MDN.

metrics.name: Resource caps enforced
metrics.good: Memory and time caps set and enforced for every tier
metrics.method: Per-tier preset in platform config; numeric defaults to be set after benchmarking.
metrics.basis: SES explicitly leaves exhaustion unmitigated; QuickJS provides the knobs.

metrics.name: Pyodide cold-start time and download size
metrics.good: unverified: to be benchmarked
metrics.method: Measure first load and warm load on campus network; npm core package unpacked size is 13,879,282 bytes (core only).
metrics.basis: No sourced figure for end-to-end cold start.

metrics.name: Release provenance
metrics.good: 100% of community releases built in CI with signed provenance
metrics.method: Verify attestations before listing; npm provenance links a package to source and build and is signed via Sigstore.
metrics.basis: Provenance proves origin, not safety.

visualization: Install-time permission card in plain language with icons (reads geometry: yes; network: none; storage: none; CPU/memory caps) modelled on browser extension permission warnings.
Per-node runtime badge: tier T0-T3, shield colour for 'reviewed' vs 'unreviewed community', small live meters for CPU ms and memory.
Red 'terminated' banner with reason; sandbox report log with denied calls.
modules.method: First-party modules run in a trusted worker. Community modules run in a dedicated Worker created inside an iframe on a separate sandbox origin (sandbox attribute, no allow-same-origin). The worker response carries its own CSP (connect-src none). The only API is postMessage/MessagePort; Layer 0 data is passed as transferred copies. A watchdog calls Worker.terminate on timeout. T1: QuickJS-WASM with memory, stack and interrupt limits, or SES Compartments with frozen intrinsics. T2: Pyodide with ctypes blocked, Emscripten exports stripped, import allowlist, no network, inside the isolated worker, enabled only after maintainer review. T3 (roadmap): server job in a gVisor or microVM sandbox, no network, no secrets. A red-team test suite runs in CI for each tier.

libraries.name: quickjs-emscripten 0.32.0
libraries.role: T1: untrusted JS in WASM with memory, stack and deadline limits

libraries.name: ses 2.3.0 (Endo)
libraries.role: T1 alternative: Hardened JS compartments

libraries.name: Pyodide 314.0.7
libraries.role: T2: Python in WASM, only inside host isolation

libraries.name: @extism/extism 2.0.0-rc13
libraries.role: WASM plug-in framework with limiters (release candidate)

libraries.name: coi-serviceworker
libraries.role: COOP/COEP on static hosts

libraries.name: gVisor (runsc)
libraries.role: T3: user-space kernel for container isolation

modules.effort: v1: T0 plus T1 about 2 dev-weeks; hardened T2 about 2 more weeks; T3 roadmap, 4+ weeks (team estimate).
modules.human_judgment: Maintainers decide which tier and permissions a module may have, review T2 code, triage vulnerability reports and decide takedowns.
modules.limits: No browser sandbox is a proven boundary against every attack: side channels and SharedArrayBuffer timers remain possible per the WebAssembly and SES documentation. Pyodide hardening is an arms race; two of the seven products in the Aug 2026 disclosure got no fix because maintainers left isolation to deployers. COEP effects on embeds are unverified.
jury_criteria: No direct jury criterion; protects entrants' unpublished designs, which VTC rules require to stay anonymous until judging.

modules.name: Registry and distribution
modules.design_question: How should modules be published, reviewed, versioned, forked and installed so the community can share them GitHub-style while maintainers keep quality and security?
inputs: Pull request adding a module version (manifest, bundle, tests)
Maintainer review decisions and CI results
outputs: Registry index: one JSON-lines file per module id, one line per version {version, bundle URL, SHA-256, dependency ranges, tier, permissions, yanked, forked_from}
Installable bundles with provenance attestations
Fork lineage graph and workspace lockfile entries

parameters.name: index_model (git index repo | sparse static JSON)
parameters.relationship: A git index gives reviewable history and zero server cost; sparse per-file fetching lowers client download. Cargo supports both; Homebrew taps are plain git repositories installed by name.

parameters.name: review_gate (CI plus human approval)
parameters.relationship: Homebrew merges only after CI passes and an organisation member approves; Obsidian review is automated and blocks installation until errors are fixed; Yak describes no review step. Stricter gate -> higher quality, slower publishing.

parameters.name: immutability and yank
parameters.relationship: A published version is never edited; yanking sets a flag so new installs skip it while existing pinned graphs still resolve (Cargo yanked flag; Comfy and Yak versions cannot be overwritten).

parameters.name: version resolution and lockfile
parameters.relationship: Exact pins in the lockfile keep results reproducible; ranges apply to dependencies only. ComfyUI stores node versions in workflow JSON for the same reason.

parameters.name: fork lineage (forked_from)
parameters.relationship: A fork is a separate repository linked to its upstream; forks in a network share git data, and upstream owners can read all forks -> lineage and licence continuity can be tracked.

parameters.name: naming and namespace
parameters.relationship: Case-insensitive collision checks and treating '-' and '_' as equal reduce confusing or look-alike names (crates.io rules).

parameters.name: hosting limits
parameters.relationship: GitHub Pages allows a 1 GB published site and a 100 GB/month soft bandwidth limit; larger assets such as Python wheels must come from a CDN.

metrics.name: CI gate before merge
metrics.good: 100% of merged module PRs passed all automated checks
metrics.method: Branch protection requires status checks and a CODEOWNERS review.
metrics.basis: Homebrew contributing guide: pull requests with failing CI should not be merged.

metrics.name: Time to first maintainer response
metrics.good: <= 3 days
metrics.method: Median interval from PR open to first non-bot response.
metrics.basis: Editable preset; CHAOSS defines the metric and says to exclude bot replies but gives no numeric bands.

metrics.name: SemVer breaking-change detection
metrics.good: Every schema-breaking change shipped as MAJOR
metrics.bad: Breaking change shipped as MINOR or PATCH
metrics.method: Automated manifest diff in CI (P15-M03).
metrics.basis: SemVer 2.0.0.

metrics.name: Published registry size
metrics.good: <= 1 GB
metrics.method: Measure the Pages artifact in CI.
metrics.basis: GitHub Pages published-site limit.

metrics.name: Releases with signed provenance
metrics.method: CI verifies attestation before the index line is accepted.
metrics.basis: npm provenance mechanism; threshold is our policy.

metrics.name: Flagged or yanked versions shown with reason in the client
metrics.method: Client integration test against flags.json and the yanked field.
metrics.basis: Course requirement that wrong claims stay visible.

visualization: Registry grid with filters by category code, phase, jury tag, licence and status; cards show version, SPDX badge, tests pass/fail, counts of verified and team-assumption thresholds, expert-reviewed badge.
Module detail page: README, manifest summary, source list, version timeline with yanked and FALSE ASSUMPTION markers, dependents.
Fork lineage drawn as a DAG; PR review checklist sidebar with CI status badges.
Install button adds module@version to the workspace lockfile.
modules.method: The registry is a public GitHub repository (index repo) with one JSON-lines file per module id and one line per version, following the Cargo index layout. An author opens a PR adding a version line; CI runs manifest lint (P15-M03), fixtures, the sandbox red-team smoke test (P15-M04), the SPDX licence check and the source-link check; a CODEOWNERS maintainer approves; merge publishes the index through GitHub Pages. Bundles are built by GitHub Actions with provenance attestations. Clients resolve exact versions into a workspace lockfile. Yanking flips a flag; other fields never change. Forks are repositories with forked_from and their own index lines.

libraries.name: GitHub Actions + npm provenance / Sigstore (sigstore 5.0.0)
libraries.role: Signed build provenance for module releases

libraries.name: semver 7.8.5
libraries.role: Range resolution

libraries.name: ajv 8.20.0
libraries.role: Index line validation in CI

libraries.name: github/github-mcp-server
libraries.role: MCP server letting Claude Code read repos and open or review index PRs

libraries.name: Cargo registry index format; Homebrew tap model
libraries.role: Index layout and tap-style distribution models

modules.effort: v1: about 2-3 dev-weeks for index repo, CI, browse UI and install flow (team estimate).
modules.human_judgment: Maintainers judge scope fit, duplication, quality of sources, merge and yank decisions.
modules.limits: A static registry has no server-side rate limiting or private modules; Pages bandwidth is a soft cap; the PR queue is a maintainer bottleneck. Provenance proves where code was built, not that it is safe. Typosquatting and look-alike names are only partly addressed. Food4Rhino could not be opened, so its review and rating practices are not used as evidence.
jury_criteria: No direct jury criterion; enabler for all four tags through community-contributed evaluation modules.

modules.name: Comments, reviews, ratings and flags
modules.design_question: How do users comment on, review, rate and flag modules or single thresholds so wrong assumptions stay visible, corrections are traceable, and ratings are not misleading?
inputs: Flag submissions {module@version, threshold id, claim, evidence URL, proposed correction, flag type}
outputs: Rating summary {n, positive fraction, Wilson lower bound}
Flag records with status, affected versions and corrected value
Chip colour state per threshold; moderation queue

parameters.name: rating_score (Wilson lower bound, z = 1.96)
parameters.relationship: Small samples inflate plain averages; the lower bound ranks 2 of 2 positive ratings at about 0.34 and 180 of 200 at about 0.85 (computed from the formula), so thinly rated modules do not outrank well-tested ones.

parameters.name: min_votes_to_display
parameters.relationship: Below a minimum n the interval is wide, so show 'not enough ratings' instead of a number.

parameters.name: flag_taxonomy (FALSE_ASSUMPTION | UNVERIFIED | UNRESOLVED | TEAM_ASSUMPTION)
parameters.relationship: A flagged claim is never deleted; the record keeps affected versions and the fixed version, as OSV records introduced, fixed and withdrawn events for advisories.

parameters.name: discussion_backend (giscus on GitHub Discussions | own database)
parameters.relationship: giscus stores threads in GitHub Discussions, needs no database and moderates on GitHub, but users need GitHub accounts; own database removes that dependency at the cost of hosting and moderation tooling.

parameters.name: moderator_response_time
parameters.relationship: Longer time to first response -> lower perceived activity and weaker contributor retention (CHAOSS objective; no numeric relationship given).

parameters.name: expert vs crowd separation
parameters.relationship: Crowd ratings measure perceived usefulness; expert review (P15-M08) measures correctness. Showing them separately prevents a popular but wrong module looking verified. Design logic.

metrics.name: Wilson lower-bound rating
metrics.method: Count positive and negative votes; apply the Wilson score formula at 95% confidence.
metrics.basis: Formula and z = 1.96 verified; the good/bad cut-offs and minimum n are editable team presets.

metrics.name: Time to first response to comments and flags
metrics.good: <= 3 days
metrics.method: CHAOSS Time to First Response, excluding bot replies.
metrics.basis: Definition verified; bands are presets.

metrics.name: Flag completeness
metrics.good: Every FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag has evidence URL, corrected value and affected version range
metrics.method: Issue form validation plus maintainer checklist.
metrics.basis: Modelled on the OSV schema fields.

metrics.name: Flag visibility
metrics.good: 100% of flags render in their reserved colour with an icon and text label
metrics.method: UI test; contrast of the flag colour at least 3:1.
metrics.basis: Course requirement (flagged claims stay visible); WCAG non-text contrast.

visualization: Per-threshold chip: green verified, amber team assumption, grey unverified, reserved magenta-red FALSE ASSUMPTION with the old value struck through and the corrected value beside it; hover shows the source and flag history.
Rating histogram with a Wilson-interval whisker and an 'n' label.
Version strip showing affected and fixed version range, in OSV style.
Embedded giscus thread under each module; moderation queue for maintainers.
modules.method: Each module page embeds a giscus thread mapped to the module id. Structured reviews are discussion replies using a template (vote plus evidence link); a GitHub Action parses them into ratings.json. Ratings count positives and negatives and compute the Wilson lower bound with z = 1.96, hiding the score below the minimum n. Flags come from an Issue form that records {module@version, threshold id, claim, evidence URL, proposed value, type}. Maintainers set status; an Action writes flags.json in the registry and never deletes entries. The client overlays flags on threshold chips. A confirmed false claim keeps the old value visible (struck) and links to the corrected version, with status false_assumption_corrected. The expert-reviewed badge is separate (P15-M08).

modules.name: Workflow templates and on/off toggles
modules.design_question: How can users save, share and fork whole graphs as templates, pin module versions for reproducibility, and switch modules on or off without silently breaking downstream results?
outputs: Template package: graph.json, lockfile.json, README, LICENSE, preview image, requires.json (Layer 0 port types and units)
Enabled-state map and dependency-impact report
Resolved/unresolved module list

parameters.name: lockfile pins (module@exact version)
parameters.relationship: Pinning keeps results reproducible when a module later changes; ComfyUI stores node versions in workflow JSON so workflows can be reproduced.

parameters.name: toggle semantics (bypass | block | remove)
parameters.relationship: Bypass keeps downstream nodes computing on different inputs; block marks them stale; remove deletes wires. The choice changes whether downstream metrics still mean what the user thinks. Design logic.

parameters.name: template_jury_tags
parameters.relationship: Tagging a template with the jury criteria its modules evidence shows entrants which of the 40/30/20/10 weights the graph can support; it does not measure design quality.

parameters.name: template licence
parameters.relationship: Graph JSON and docs are content (CC BY 4.0 suits); code keeps an OSI licence. Creative Commons advises against CC licences for software.

parameters.name: embedded third-party material
parameters.relationship: Embedding brief text or images would redistribute copyrighted material; link and cite instead. VTC terms leave entrants' rights with entrants and state no licence to redistribute the brief.

parameters.name: anonymity of exports
parameters.relationship: Board exports must not carry author or team identifiers; VTC terms require submissions free of identifying marks.

metrics.name: Template reproducibility
metrics.good: 100% identical output hashes on re-run with pinned versions
metrics.method: Import template, resolve lockfile, run twice, compare RunRecords.
metrics.basis: Course requirement of showing work; threshold is our policy.

metrics.name: Dependency resolvability
metrics.good: 100% of pinned modules resolve; yanked versions warned
metrics.method: Resolve each pin against the registry index.
metrics.basis: Policy; yank semantics from Cargo index.

metrics.name: Unwired required inputs
metrics.method: Static graph check against manifests.
metrics.basis: Policy.

metrics.name: Silent breakage after toggling off
metrics.good: 0 downstream nodes left unmarked
metrics.method: Reachability from the toggled node; all descendants must show stale or blocked.
metrics.basis: Policy.

metrics.name: Identifying strings in export metadata
metrics.method: Scan exported image/PDF metadata and filenames for author, team, institution, path.
metrics.basis: VTC terms: submissions must not show marks identifying the author (section 5.1).

visualization: Template gallery cards: graph thumbnail, jury-tag dots, module count, licence badge.
Template detail: dependency list with lock status and flag chips.
On/off switch on every node; on toggle, descendants turn hatched with a banner 'n results depend on this module'.
Graph diff view for forks.
modules.method: A template is an archive of graph.json (nodes with module id@exact version, parameters, enabled flags; edges), lockfile.json, README.md, LICENSE, preview.png and requires.json. Importing resolves each pinned module from the registry, warns on yanked or flagged versions (P15-M06) and runs lint (P15-M03). Toggling sets enabled=false; the scheduler (P15-M02) applies the node's mode and the UI computes descendants by reachability to display impact. Forking a template copies it with forked_from. Export-for-boards strips author, team and path metadata and scans embedded metadata. Templates are published through the same index-repo pattern as modules, with category 'template'.

Community-health checklist and Scorecard result

parameters.name: governance_model (BDFL | meritocracy | liberal contribution)
parameters.relationship: A small student-run project can start with named maintainers and a written contributor process, formalising later; documenting how someone becomes a maintainer in GOVERNANCE.md reduces the 'private clique' perception.

parameters.name: code_of_conduct text and version
parameters.relationship: Contributor Covenant 3.0 is CC BY-SA 4.0, so derived conduct texts must share alike; it needs a real reporting contact and an enforcement ladder (warning, limited activities, suspension, ban).

parameters.name: code vs content licence
parameters.relationship: Code under an OSI-approved licence (MIT or Apache-2.0); documentation and templates under CC BY 4.0. Creative Commons recommends against CC licences for software and allows them for documentation and artistic elements.

parameters.name: review depth for the expert-reviewed badge
parameters.relationship: rOpenSci uses two external reviewers in a public thread; JOSS checks OSI licence, tests and documentation. More reviewers -> more confidence but longer lead time; the optimal number has no evidence.

parameters.name: CODEOWNERS and branch protection
parameters.relationship: Requiring a code-owner review makes an owner of each path approve changes to it; owners need write access or their approval is not requested.

parameters.name: AI-use disclosure
parameters.relationship: Homebrew requires disclosure of AI/LLM use and personal accountability for generated content; JOSS has an AI policy for reviews.

parameters.name: Indigenous-knowledge and data policy
parameters.relationship: CARE principles (collective benefit, authority to control, responsibility, ethics) imply that modules or data touching Indigenous cultural knowledge need consent and attribution checks before listing.

parameters.name: brief and third-party redistribution
parameters.relationship: Do not upload the VTC PDF or site model; store citations and derived parameters. No redistribution licence for the brief is stated, so treat it as all rights reserved (team assumption).

metrics.name: GitHub community-profile completeness
metrics.good: README, code of conduct, CONTRIBUTING, LICENSE, security policy and issue templates all present
metrics.method: Read the repository's community profile.
metrics.basis: GitHub community profile checklist.

metrics.name: OpenSSF Scorecard aggregate
metrics.method: Run Scorecard on the registry and tool repositories in CI.
metrics.basis: Scale 0-10 and check weights verified; the cut-offs are editable presets.

metrics.name: Expert-reviewed badge criteria
metrics.good: >= 2 independent reviewers with declared expertise, public review thread, passing tests, OSI licence
metrics.bad: Badge shown without a thread or with fewer than 2 reviewers
metrics.method: Badge is issued only when a review record exists and links to the thread.
metrics.basis: Practice taken from rOpenSci (two reviewers, badge links to thread) and JOSS (OSI licence, tests); adopting it here is our decision.

metrics.name: Licence audit
metrics.good: 100% of modules have a valid SPDX licence and compatible dependency licences
metrics.method: Parse manifests and dependency trees.
metrics.basis: SPDX list; a missing licence leaves no reuse right.

metrics.name: Copyrighted brief files in the registry
metrics.method: Hash and filename scan against the VTC downloads.
metrics.basis: Precaution: no redistribution licence stated.

visualization: Governance dashboard: health checklist with ticks linked to the files on GitHub, Scorecard gauge 0-10.
Badge on each module card: 'Expert-reviewed' (tooltip lists reviewers, expertise, date and links to the review thread), 'First-party', or none.
Licence matrix table: component x licence x SPDX id x OSI flag.
modules.method: Adopt one repository skeleton: LICENSE (code), LICENSE-content (CC BY 4.0), CONTRIBUTING (module PR checklist: manifest, sources opened, tests, licence, AI-use disclosure), CODE_OF_CONDUCT (Contributor Covenant with a real contact and a backup recipient), GOVERNANCE (maintainer roles and how to join), SECURITY, CODEOWNERS per category. Expert review: maintainers invite two reviewers with relevant expertise; review happens in a public thread against a checklist (sources open, thresholds correct, relationship statements true, tests pass); on approval a review record is added to the registry and the badge links to the thread. CI runs Scorecard and the licence audit. Content from Indigenous communities is held until consent and attribution are confirmed.

sources.title: Grasshopper data trees and Python
sources.extract: A tree maps paths to branches; branches hold items; paths can be sparse. The page does not cover item/list/tree access types.

sources.title: Topological sorting
sources.extract: Ordering exists iff the graph is acyclic; Kahn and DFS algorithms run in O(V+E); leftover edges or a temporary-marked revisit reveal a cycle.

sources.title: Pyodide repository
sources.extract: CPython port to WebAssembly; MPL-2.0; in a browser Python has full access to Web APIs; no sandbox statement on the page.

sources.title: Pyodide - Using Pyodide in a web worker
sources.extract: Pyodide needs a module-type worker; the main thread posts messages with ids; workers cannot touch the DOM or share globals.

sources.title: Pyodide - Keyboard interrupts
sources.extract: Interrupt with a SharedArrayBuffer passed to setInterruptBuffer; must run in a worker; server must send the headers SharedArrayBuffer requires.

sources.title: Sandcastles, Not Sandboxes: How One Architectural Flaw Exposed Seven Products
sources.extract: Published 7 Aug 2026: Python-level denylists in Pyodide sandboxes missed ctypes and Emscripten exports; seven products affected (n8n CVE-2025-68668 CVSS 9.9, Grist, cohere-terrarium, smolagents, langchain-sandbox, stlite, cibuildwheel); mitigations: allowlist, strip exports, OS-level isolation, least privilege; Python controls are an additional control, not the sole boundary.

sources.title: MDN - Using Web Workers
sources.extract: Workers have no DOM access and communicate by structured clone; they are generally not governed by the creating document's CSP (set a CSP header on the worker script response; blob/data workers inherit).

sources.title: MDN - iframe element (sandbox attribute)
sources.extract: Without allow-same-origin content gets a unique opaque origin; allow-scripts plus allow-same-origin on same-origin content lets it remove the sandbox; serve untrusted content from a separate origin.

sources.title: MDN - Window.crossOriginIsolated
sources.extract: Cross-origin isolation requires COOP same-origin and COEP require-corp or credentialless; needed to use SharedArrayBuffer.

sources.title: MDN - Worker.terminate()
sources.extract: Immediately stops a Web Worker without letting it finish pending operations.

sources.title: WebAssembly - Security
sources.extract: Modules run in fault-isolated sandboxes with bounds-checked linear memory and control-flow integrity; side channels, race conditions and overflows within linear memory remain possible.

sources.title: SES (Secure ECMAScript) - Endo
sources.extract: lockdown() freezes intrinsics; Compartments start with no ambient authority; limits: guests can run forever and allocate unlimited memory; availability and exhaustion threats not mitigated. Repository licence shown as Apache-2.0.

sources.title: quickjs-emscripten
sources.extract: QuickJS compiled to WebAssembly; memory limits, stack limits and interrupt/deadline handlers; host functions exposed explicitly; MIT per npm.

sources.title: Extism
sources.extract: BSD-3-Clause; plug-in framework on WebAssembly for untrusted code; JS host SDK for web, Node, Deno, Bun; runtime limiters and timers (details not given).

sources.title: Deno - Security and permissions
sources.extract: Default-deny permissions; --allow-run and --allow-ffi are equivalent to allow-all; for untrusted code use layered defence: minimal permissions, Web Worker, OS sandboxing, and gVisor or Firecracker VMs.

sources.title: coi-serviceworker
sources.extract: MIT; enables COOP/COEP via service worker on hosts such as GitHub Pages that cannot set headers; must be a separate same-origin file; first load triggers a reload.

sources.title: Chrome extensions - Permission warnings
sources.extract: Permissions declared in the manifest; some trigger install-time warnings; optional permissions requested at runtime; an update adding a warned permission disables the extension until accepted.

sources.title: VS Code - Extension manifest
sources.extract: package.json fields: lowercase unique name, SemVer version, publisher, engines.vscode (not *), fixed categories list, activationEvents, contributes, license.

sources.title: JSON Schema specification
sources.extract: Current version is 2020-12 (previous 2019-09); Core and Validation specifications plus meta-schemas.

sources.title: Ajv JSON Schema validator
sources.extract: MIT; supports drafts 2020-12, 2019-09, 07 (04 via separate package); fast validator for Node.js and browsers.

sources.title: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0
sources.extract: Declare a public API; MAJOR for incompatible changes, MINOR for compatible features, PATCH for fixes; 0.y.z is initial development; released versions must not be modified.

sources.title: Cargo - Registry index format
sources.extract: Git or sparse index; one file per package with one JSON line per version (vers, deps, cksum, yanked); entries immutable except yanked; crates.io naming rules (case-insensitive collisions, '-' and '_' equivalent).

sources.title: Homebrew - How to create and maintain a tap
sources.extract: A tap is a git repository of formulae (name homebrew-*); install via brew install user/repo/formula; non-official taps need trust; semantic version tags recommended.

sources.title: homebrew-core CONTRIBUTING

sources.title: Obsidian - Submit your plugin

sources.title: Yak - The package manifest

sources.title: Yak - Pushing a package to the server

sources.title: Comfy Registry - Overview

sources.title: npm - Generating provenance statements

sources.title: GitHub Docs - About forks

sources.title: giscus

sources.title: How Not To Sort By Average Rating
sources.extract: Wilson score lower bound = [p + z^2/2n - z*sqrt((p(1-p) + z^2/4n)/n)] / (1 + z^2/n); z = 1.96 for 95% confidence.

sources.title: web.dev - Interaction to Next Paint (INP)

flags.claim: Pyodide/WebAssembly isolation is enough to run untrusted community Python safely in the browser.
flags.correction: Treat Pyodide as one layer only. A 7 Aug 2026 disclosure showed escapes in seven products (ctypes and Emscripten exports reached the JS host). Add host-level isolation (separate origin, worker CSP, no network), allowlists, stripped exports, maintainer review, or run server-side in a sandbox.
flags.detail: WebAssembly's own docs list side channels and in-memory overflows as remaining risks; two of the seven products received no fix because maintainers treated isolation as the deployer's job.

flags.claim: A Web Worker created by our page inherits the page's Content-Security-Policy and is therefore a safe place for community code.
flags.correction: Workers are generally not governed by the creating document's CSP; a worker script must be served with its own CSP header (blob: and data: workers inherit). Workers also still have network access unless blocked.
flags.detail: MDN: a page with script-src 'self' blocks eval(), yet code in a worker it creates can still call eval().

flags.claim: litegraph.js (or its Comfy fork) is a maintained, safe choice for the node canvas.
flags.correction: Original litegraph.js last pushed 2024-08-01 with about 1.2 k weekly downloads; the Comfy-Org fork is archived (2026-01-14). Use @xyflow/react (pushed 2026-10-20, about 8.3 M weekly downloads) with Rete as the fallback.
flags.detail: Observed 21 Oct 2026 from GitHub API and npm download API.

flags.claim: MIT licensing of React Flow means the on-canvas attribution can be removed without paying.
flags.detail: The vendor states attribution may be removed only with a Pro subscription (Starter $169/month, Professional $289/month) while the library itself stays MIT. Whether MIT legally obliges the on-canvas badge was not verified; default is to leave it visible.

flags.claim: The Contributor Covenant text is CC BY 4.0.

flags.detail: Pick one version and record its licence in the repo; a share-alike text constrains derivative conduct documents.

flags.detail: Shown in the tool as editable team assumptions per the course rule; replace with sourced values when found.

Template granularity (nodes per template) vs reuse and learning: no sourced evidence.
Disabled-node mode (bypass vs block) vs correctness of downstream verdicts: design logic only, not empirically sourced.

case_studies.tool: Grasshopper ecosystem: Yak package manager and Food4Rhino
case_studies.what_it_does: Yak packages Grasshopper plug-ins with a manifest.yml (name, version, authors, description), installs them through Rhino's Package Manager, and lets owners push versions that cannot be overwritten, only yanked. Food4Rhino is the named community download site.
case_studies.workflow_step: Distribution and discovery of analysis plug-ins
case_studies.how_used: Designers find a plug-in, install it, wire it into a definition by hand.
case_studies.strengths: Simple manifest, SemVer or four-digit versions, immutable versions with yank, ownership by first pusher.
case_studies.stops_at: The Yak push page describes no review or moderation step and no sandbox; it records no per-threshold sources or assumptions. Food4Rhino could not be opened.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Automated manifest lint, source-link checking and test running before listing.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Judging whether a plug-in's thresholds are right for Vancouver policy.

case_studies.what_it_does: Public registry of custom nodes with semantic versioning, immutable published versions, deprecation, globally unique names, malicious-behaviour scanning with a verification flag, and workflow JSON that stores node versions.
case_studies.how_used: Users install nodes through ComfyUI-Manager and share workflows.
case_studies.strengths: Closest precedent for a node canvas with community modules, versioned workflows and a security verification flag.
case_studies.stops_at: Scanning looks for patterns such as custom pip wheels and arbitrary system calls; the page does not claim it proves safety or describe runtime sandboxing. Licence and pyproject requirements were not on the page.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Pattern-based scanning and triage of new versions.

case_studies.what_it_does: Plugins ship README, LICENSE and manifest.json; version must match the release tag; ids are unique; submission through the directory with automatic review that blocks installation until errors are fixed.
case_studies.how_used: Author publishes a GitHub release, submits, fixes automated review errors.
case_studies.stops_at: The page describes automatic review only; no human expert review or sandbox is described.

case_studies.what_it_does: Taps are git repositories of formulae installable by name; homebrew-core accepts changes by pull request with CI, organisation-member approval and bot merge; AI/LLM use must be disclosed.
case_studies.workflow_step: Index repository, PR review, forks and third-party taps
case_studies.how_used: Maintainers review PRs; users add third-party taps and must trust them.
case_studies.strengths: Reviewable git history, CI gate, clear maintainer approval, tap model for unofficial sources.
case_studies.stops_at: Non-official taps rely on user trust; the pages do not describe sandboxing of formula code.

case_studies.tool: rOpenSci software peer review and JOSS
case_studies.what_it_does: Public, expert peer review of software: rOpenSci uses two external reviewers and gives a badge linking to the review thread; JOSS checks OSI licence, tests, documentation and development history.
case_studies.how_used: Authors submit; reviewers work through a checklist in a public GitHub thread.
case_studies.strengths: Transparent, named reviewers, badge points to evidence.
case_studies.stops_at: Neither source defines reviewer qualifications in a way we can copy; both review software quality, not architectural correctness.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Pre-filling the checklist (licence, tests, links) for reviewers.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Expert judgment on wind, structure or planning thresholds.

case_studies.tool: Node-canvas libraries: React Flow (xyflow) vs Rete vs Baklava vs litegraph
case_studies.what_it_does: React Flow renders custom nodes, handles and validation hooks; Rete adds a pull-based dataflow engine with caching; Baklava is Vue-based with an engine and interface types; litegraph.js is canvas-based with typed slots.
case_studies.how_used: Embedded as the editor and, for Rete and Baklava, the engine.
case_studies.strengths: All MIT. xyflow has by far the largest use (about 8.3 M weekly downloads) and active pushes; Rete has a built-in cached dataflow engine.
case_studies.stops_at: React Flow provides no execution engine or domain port typing (app code); litegraph.js is stale and its Comfy fork archived; Baklava has small adoption.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Deciding what the port-type vocabulary should be.
case_studies.license_cost: MIT for all four; React Flow Pro is optional and starts at $169/month for attribution removal.
